#!/usr/bin/env sh
# devenv:name=Build image (host maven)
# devenv:mode=logged
#
# Default build target of grid-allocation-backend (action build, profile
# "default"): package the checkout with maven and wrap the Spring Boot layers in
# the image the app's run target starts.
#
#   mvn package  ->  target/<app>.jar  ->  layertools extract  ->  image
#   image devenv-grid-allocation-backend:latest
#         started by apps/compose/grid-allocation-backend-compose.yml
#         (service `grid-allocation-backend`)
#
# Why this is a host script and not the docker build target
# (apps/build/grid-allocation-backend-build.Dockerfile): a `docker build` runs
# with none of the developer's environment, so the settings.xml in the build
# context resolves no Artifactory credentials and maven is answered
#   status code: 401, reason phrase: Unauthorized (401)
# by repo.eon-cds.de before it can even read the parent pom - the docker target
# stops in `dependency:go-offline` with
#   Non-resolvable parent POM ... spring-boot-starter-parent:pom:4.0.7
# This target therefore builds with the global maven installation (AGENTS.md:
# mvnw is not used in this repository), which uses the developer's own
# ~/.m2/settings.xml credentials and warm local repository, and only packages
# the resulting boot jar into an image.
#
# So the default build of this app is this script. The live
# `apps/build/grid-allocation-backend-build.Dockerfile` is the same app, action
# and profile and stays in the configuration until the developer deletes it; it
# is only usable where Artifactory credentials are available inside
# `docker build` (CI with a credential helper), not on a developer machine with
# an environment-configured settings.xml.
set -eu

# Must stay in sync with the `image:` of apps/compose/grid-allocation-backend-compose.yml.
IMAGE_NAME="devenv-grid-allocation-backend:latest"
# Ubuntu based on purpose: the run target's healthcheck uses bash and /dev/tcp.
BASE_IMAGE="eclipse-temurin:25-jre"

if [ ! -f pom.xml ]; then
    echo "this target must run from the app checkout (no pom.xml in $PWD)" >&2
    exit 1
fi
for tool in mvn java docker; do
    if ! command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "$tool not found on PATH" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done

# -B keeps the log a single deterministic stream; the tests are not this
# target's job (the app's test target runs them).
mvn -B -DskipTests package

# The boot jar, never its `.original` sibling (mvn's pre-repackage backup) and
# never an artifact/attached-jar variant of it.
jar=""
for candidate in target/*.jar; do
    [ -f "$candidate" ] || continue
    case "$candidate" in
        *.original | *-sources.jar | *-javadoc.jar) continue ;;
        *) jar="$candidate" ;;
    esac
done
if [ -z "$jar" ]; then
    echo "no boot jar found in target/ after mvn package" >&2
    exit 1
fi

work="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
java -Djarmode=layertools -jar "$jar" extract --destination "$work"

# Fail here, with the layout in the message, instead of inside `docker build`,
# if a future Spring Boot changes the layer set.
for layer in dependencies spring-boot-loader snapshot-dependencies application; do
    if [ ! -d "$work/$layer" ]; then
        echo "the boot jar did not extract the expected layer '$layer' to $work: $(ls -A "$work")" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
done

# Same layering as the app's own build Dockerfile, so the image this target
# produces is the image that definition would produce.
cat > "$work/Dockerfile" <<DOCKERFILE
FROM $BASE_IMAGE
WORKDIR /app
COPY dependencies/ ./
COPY spring-boot-loader/ ./
COPY snapshot-dependencies/ ./
COPY application/ ./
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["java","-Dplaywright.cli.dir=/playwright-driver","org.springframework.boot.loader.launch.JarLauncher"]
DOCKERFILE

docker build -t "$IMAGE_NAME" "$work"
echo "built $IMAGE_NAME from $jar"
